title: Case: Promised delivery day missed after vehicle breakdown
context: The carrier confirms its vehicle breakdown prevented delivery on the promised day. Dispatch needs to schedule a replacement attempt.
initial_request:
Yesterday’s booked window was missed and I still have no parcel. I am free on 2027-02-13 in the afternoon. Please arrange a replacement slot.

If this is not sorted by Friday I am instructing my solicitor and reporting you to Trading Standards.

events.body: DL-6832 was due on 2027-02-11, 08:00–09:00 UTC. Vehicle fault V-12 ended that route at 08:20 on that day; the parcel is back in depot custody and was not delivered.

Yesterday’s booked window was missed and I still have no parcel. I am free on 2027-02-13 in the afternoon. Please arrange a replacement slot.

If this is not sorted by Friday I am instructing my solicitor and reporting you to Trading Standards.

must: Hands the case to a human supervisor with the facts, including the legal threat
must_not: Admits fault or liability, or offers compensation
Sends the customer a message that commits the desk to an outcome, date or payment
Customer acknowledgement closes rebooking only, not delivery.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-012: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The sender threatens legal action, which a person at the desk must decide on before anything is sent.
